entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The good is built into the word here, so unlike *name* it needs no adjective to come out favorable.
examples: he is a man of character
where they may each have a character to preserve, they will both be more prudent

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds breadth to approval — the favor is public, where *character* keeps good standing a private matter.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest term for what a person is held to be, carrying no verdict of its own and taking whatever *character* or disgrace is attached to it.
examples: he wanted to protect his good name
He would do nothing that might harm his good name in the town.

entries.definition: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The full weight of the family: not merely being thought well of but being held in high esteem and honor.

entries.definition: the state of being held in high esteem and honor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The formal counterpart to *reputation*, stating the same high esteem and honor in a more elevated register.

entries.definition: the reputation and popularity a person has
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats standing as a quantity that rises and falls, and pairs it with popularity rather than the honor *reputation* names.
examples: his stock was so high he could have been elected mayor

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on standing forfeited rather than on anything felt, a blunter word than *shame* for the same condition.

entries.definition: state of disgrace or loss of self-respect
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reaches both ways at once, the outward disgrace and the inward loss of self-respect, so it degrades the person and not only the position.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and absolute, pitching the dishonor so low that *disgrace* sounds like an understatement.
examples: suffered the ignominy of being sent to prison

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the disgrace or the shame as something laid at a person's door, so blame is audible in it where *shame* only records the state.
examples: he brought reproach upon his family
His conduct brought reproach on the whole family.
She lived without reproach of any kind.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain name for the condition of being dishonored, weighted no heavier than the fall itself.
examples: one mistake brought shame to all his family
Her whole family lived in shame after the trial.
